items.title: fix(doctor): preserve conversations through legacy binding migration …
items.summary: fix(doctor): preserve conversations through legacy binding migration (#143347) Related: #136257 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Doctor leaves old Claude conversation IDs outside the canonical binding, while runtime lookup and normal saves still depend on the retired field. The upgrade must preserve locked-session continuity and prevent deliberately cleared stale conversations from returning. ## Why This Change Was Made This follows the approved Doctor migration and reader-retirement scope from #136257. Doctor copies safe legacy IDs before removing the old field, and runtime lookup and normal saves change together. Existing canonical bindings, provider-keyed IDs, and resume metadata take precedence. Locked rows change only their binding representation; identity, ownership, route, and recency remain intact. Ambiguous records stay saved with reconciliation warnings. The existing stale-route repair also clears the old migration source when it clears a Claude binding. A later migration step therefore cannot restore an obsolete conversation. Historical-field cleanup and protected plugin-slot handling remain available for unresolved old records. ## User Impact Run `openclaw doctor --fix` after upgrading and before resuming sessions that only have the old field. Configured and locked conversations keep their IDs and resume metadata. Stale conversations stay cleared. Normal saves no longer recreate the retired field. ## Evidence The initial main regression failed because the canonical binding was missing after Doctor repair. The first candidate passed 74 focused tests. Public Doctor proof and the first source review then exposed two connected gaps: stale-state resurrection and locked-session continuity. Both are repaired in this revision, with the earlier failures retained. The compiled runtime built from this head passes public `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, `sessions --all-agents --json`, and repeated Doctor repair on 10 synthetic sessions across two agents. Saved state was checked after reopening both databases. Configured legacy IDs, canonical metadata, provider-keyed IDs, and locked ownership are preserved; ambiguous and empty records retain warnings; stale Claude state stays cleared. Every checked record is stable on repeat. The normal native pre-commit hook passed on the revised source. [Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34397549548) covers type checks and the updated migration, save, fork, and Doctor-to-history cases. Runtime artifact build `41b019c889c4403b33993ee39d7eb04269b73316` is the CI test merge containing head `96e5877b0f15dffe7baa9fd934cbdea07ccb694e`; those identities are kept separate in the proof. No live provider conversation, credential operation, or schema change is claimed. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi
